proof: Nine original gray cells occupy exactly five rows y2..6 and five columns x2..6. Direct shared-edge counting gives perimeter4*9-2*8=20. For any finite union of unit cells, if r rows and c columns are occupied then perimeter>=2(r+c), and area<=rc<=((r+c)/2)^2. At perimeter<=20 area<=25. The bounding5x5 square has area25 and perimeter20 and contains all nine cells, so16 is achievable and is the unique maximum. At area25 equality forces the same5 rows and5 columns, hence the complete original bounding5x5 block. This is the standard maximal reading of how many more; without maximal intent smaller additions are possible.
new_wrong_rule: Treat initial two-gray-neighbor test as a one-time independent exhaustive test. Initially exactly7 blank cells have two gray edge neighbors. Each is locally ΔP=4-2*2=0, but newly gray cells enable further cells, giving16 overall.
